title: Landlord Withholding Security Deposit in Bengaluru
raw_input: I rented a 2BHK in Koramangala Bengaluru. I gave 1 month notice on 1st October as per agreement and vacated on 31st October. My security deposit was Rs 65000. When I asked for my refund, the landlord blocked my number and told my roommate that he is deducting Rs 35000 for full house painting and Rs 30000 for minor scratches and cleaning. The house was completely clean when I handed over keys, and I have full video proof taken on 31st October.

respondent.address: Flat 302, Green View Apts, Koramangala 4th Block, Bengaluru - 560034

case_assessment.applicable_law: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 108(m) - Reasonable Wear & Tear) & Model Tenancy Act principles
case_assessment.plain_language_summary: Landlord cannot unilaterally forfeit security deposit for normal wear and tear unless explicitly detailed with written invoices. Security deposit must be refunded within 30 days of vacant possession.
statutory_provisions: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Section 108: Lessee is bound to keep property in good condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted.
Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract.
State Rent Control Acts / Model Tenancy Framework: Maximum deposit limits and mandatory settlement timeline.
remedies: Issue formal 15-day Legal Demand Notice demanding refund with 18% p.a. interest.
File petition before Rent Authority / Rent Court (where Model Tenancy Act is notified) or Civil Court (Summary Suit under Order XXXVII CPC for liquidated debt).
File Consumer Complaint if landlord is a commercial co-living company (e.g., Stanza, Zolo) under Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
evidence_checklist: Proof of initial deposit payment (bank transaction/UPI receipt)
Notice of termination given via Email/WhatsApp with date of handover
Photos/videos of the empty flat showing clean condition at handover
Keys handover acknowledgement or chat confirmation

title: E-Commerce / Electronics Non-Refund for Defective Laptop
raw_input: I ordered an Asus Gaming Laptop for Rs 58000 on 12th September from an online seller. When it arrived on 15th September, the screen was cracked and it would not boot. I immediately raised a return request with unboxing video on 16th September. The customer care kept delaying saying technician will visit. On 28th September they abruptly closed my ticket stating return window expired. They refuse to refund my Rs 58000.

respondent.name: ElectroDeals Online Retail Pvt Ltd & Platform Grievance Officer

timeline.event: I ordered an Asus Gaming Laptop for Rs 58000 on 12th September from an online seller
When it arrived on 15th September, the screen was cracked and it would not boot
I immediately raised a return request with unboxing video on 16th September
The customer care kept delaying saying technician will visit
On 28th September they abruptly closed my ticket stating return window expired
They refuse to refund my Rs 58000

case_assessment.applicable_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 & Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
case_assessment.plain_language_summary: Consumers have statutory right against deficiency in service and unfair trade practices. Sellers and marketplace platforms cannot hide behind unreasonable return policies if defective/wrong goods were delivered.
statutory_provisions: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(47): Definition of 'Unfair Trade Practice' including deceptive claims and refusing refund for defective items.
Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Section 2(11): Definition of 'Deficiency in Service'.
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 5 & 6: Mandatory grievance officer, 48-hour acknowledgement, and refund obligations.
remedies: Issue formal 15-day Legal Demand Notice to seller and e-commerce platform.
Register grievance on National Consumer Helpline (NCH / 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in / INGRAM portal).
File online complaint on e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
evidence_checklist: Tax Invoice / Order Confirmation with Order ID
Unboxing video or photographs of the defective/wrong product
Support ticket history / Email threads / Chat logs showing timely complaint
Refusal email or arbitrary ticket closure confirmation

title: Startup Withholding 2 Months Salary & Relieving Letter
raw_input: I worked as a Frontend Developer at a tech startup in Mumbai. My monthly in-hand salary was Rs 60000. I resigned on 15th August serving full 30 days notice till 15th September. The company owes me 2 months pending salary total Rs 120000. Now HR says the company has funding problems and they cannot pay my F&F or give my relieving letter. It has been 50 days.

respondent.name: NextGen FinTech Solutions Pvt Ltd (Through its Directors)
respondent.address: Unit 401, Lotus Business Park, Andheri West, Mumbai - 400053

case_assessment.domain: Unpaid Wages, Notice Pay & F&F Settlement

timeline.event: I worked as a Frontend Developer at a tech startup in Mumbai
My monthly in-hand salary was Rs 60000
I resigned on 15th August serving full 30 days notice till 15th September
The company owes me 2 months pending salary total Rs 120000
Now HR says the company has funding problems and they cannot pay my F&F or give my relieving letter

case_assessment.applicable_law: Payment of Wages Act, 1936 & Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Section 73)
case_assessment.plain_language_summary: Employers are legally obligated to disburse earned wages and clear Full & Final (F&F) settlement within statutory timelines (typically by 7th-10th of succeeding month, or within 30 days of resignation).
statutory_provisions: Payment of Wages Act, 1936, Section 5: Time of payment of wages (before expiry of 7th or 10th day).
Payment of Wages Act, 1936, Section 7: Authorized deductions only; arbitrary forfeiture is illegal.
Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73: Breach of employment agreement and recovery of dues.
remedies: Issue formal 15-day Legal Demand Notice to Managing Director and HR.
File complaint with the jurisdictional State Labour Commissioner (Conciliation Officer).
For non-workman/managerial employees, initiate civil recovery summary suit or Section 9 IBC (Insolvency) notice if company is corporate debtor (>₹1 Cr threshold) or MSME Samadhaan if eligible.
evidence_checklist: Appointment Letter / Employment Agreement showing CTC and notice terms
Bank statements showing cessation of salary credits
Resignation email, acceptance confirmation, and handover sign-off
Follow-up emails sent to HR/Finance demanding F&F settlement
